newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-VICENZA HANDED MATCH BAN FROM HOME GROUND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VICENZA HANDED MATCH BAN FROM HOME GROUND.

text.p: Italian serie A club Vicenza were banned from using their Romeo Menti stadium for one league match and fined on Wednesday because of crowd trouble during a home game against Lazio last month.
Vicenza, domestic cup finalists whose form has plunged since they led the league for the first time in their history in November, were beaten 2-0 in the March 23 game.
Several fans tried to invade the pitch 10 minutes from time. Some broke past police and one fan was grabbed as he headed for the referee. Another four were stopped in the Vicenza penalty area.
The match had to be suspended for eight minutes.

The serie sporting judge fined Vicenza 150 million lire ($90,000) and said in his report that the punishment reflected the insults hurled at match officials and coins thrown by the crowd which hit the referee and a linesman.
The referee left the stadium under a police escort.
